g1_rf1#3.killer: Peak shear the OCA must hold for as long as the phone stays open, at 60 °C, to carry the tension that pulls the crease down to ≤1 µm
g1_rf1#3.why: As written (≤1 µm), the bond has to hold about 6x the shear at which foldable OCAs already creep. The same model says ~120 N/m (0.004 % strain, 2.5 kPa peak shear) would reach the 20 µm target with about 4x margin, so the cheapest test is to tension a coupon of the stack after folding. Note that if the layers bond tightly (cold, about −20 °C) the stiffness rises about 40x and the margin goes away.

g1_rf2#1.killer: Bending strain in the solid polymer layers that still bend at the phone's small radius (cover PET or CPI, back film); the gel does not change this
g1_rf2#1.why: Even if the gel stores no shear set, the polymer films still bend at about 3x their creep-safe strain, and the polarizer saving is already in Samsung's design, so the gain is at most ~1.2x.

g1_mech#1.killer: Fraction of the 180° bend that does not recover after 8 h folded at 60 °C. The depth of a free crease is about πR·θ/8, which I checked on an exact circle.
g1_mech#1.why: A larger radius lowers strain, but the same unrecovered fraction spread over a 15.7 mm arc makes a deeper crease. It would need about 99.7 % recovery, and the measured OCA and film recoveries are 10–100x short. The 5 mm radius also pushes the folded phone past 12 mm, versus 8.9 mm for the Fold7.

g1_rf2#3.killer: Peak shear the OCA must hold for as long as the phone stays open, at 60 °C, to carry the specified 0.1 % panel tension (T = 0.001 × EA = 2.74 kN/m, shear-lag length about 48 mm)
g1_rf2#3.why: The specified 0.1 % tension loads the edge bonds about 5x above the level where certified OCAs already creep. The model says about 25x less tension would be enough, but that is a re-spec, not the idea as written.

g1_mech#2.killer: Length mismatch between the unbonded layers. The layers are bonded at both ends of the zone and the fluid carries no shear, so a 20 µm PI layer over a 15 mm free span buckles once the mismatch exceeds the clamped Euler strain π²t²/3L².
g1_mech#2.why: Bonding the layers at the zone ends means they cannot slide, so a few tens of ppm of thermal or creep mismatch buckles the free PI into a ripple that shows in reflection; the defect moves rather than disappears.

g1_ledger#1.killer: The same constraint on the thinnest unbonded layer (20 µm PI over a 10 mm strip). Folding also adds mismatch, so the claimed 0.75% strain does not hold.
g1_ledger#1.why: Because the strip ends are bonded, the layers cannot slip, so the strain relief the idea claims does not happen and the free films buckle under ordinary thermal mismatch.

g1_ledger#2.killer: Peak OCA shear at the edges, held for as long as the phone is open, at the tension needed to flatten a 20 µm, 3 mm-wide set to 2 µm. That needs T ≈ 3.9 kN/m, or about 580 N over a 151 mm fold, given a stack bending stiffness D ≥ 3.9×10⁻⁴ N·m.
g1_ledger#2.why: Closed-loop tension can mechanically flatten the crease by about 10x, but it holds about 580 N in the hinge and the OCA in near-limit shear for as long as the phone is open, well past the 10-day hold the adhesive is designed for.

g1_neg#2.killer: Tension accuracy of a cam that sets displacement rather than force. 600 N/m on a stack with Et ≈ 2.6×10⁶ N/m over a 136 mm span is a stroke of only 31 µm.
g1_neg#2.why: The tolerance and thermal drift swamp the 31 µm stroke, so the tension swings from slack to several times nominal; even at nominal tension, a 20 µm set only drops to about 8 µm, which is not invisible.
